One blocking defect and three surviving reviewer mutants: (1) merge_train.py conflicts() parses the claimnotes merge driver's `MERGE-CLAIM: resolved <path>` stderr as merge-tree output, because Tick.git (orchestrator_tick.py ~288-290) returns stdout+stderr; in any clone with the driver installed a claim-only DIRTY gives conflicts() -> None and the tick says 'git merge-tree could not answer' and never offers the claimnotes repair; a content-plus-claim conflict lists the MERGE-CLAIM line as a conflicted file. Repair: read stdout alone (or drop non-path lines) and decide explicitly what a driver-resolved claim file means for a GitHub DIRTY (which reads [] locally); pin it with a self-test arm in a throwaway repository WITH the claimnotes driver configured (tests/throwaway_git.py; the current arm has no driver and the tick arm is stubbed), plus a mutant per behaviour. (2) mutant R2: `getattr(self, "_req_pr", None) or required` -> `required` survives: pin that the tick's NOT REVIEWABLE line includes PR_ONLY contexts (a red pr-contract at a PR head must be flagged). (3) R1: dropping the `(code == 1) != (len(lines) > 1)` guard in conflicts() survives; R3: re-running a shared workflow run once per check-run name instead of once per run survives; R4: removing the `runs is None` unreadable arm in the overlap gate survives. Each gets a pinning arm or a justified refusal in the body.
